newsitem.title: USA: Shalala seeks to reassure U.S. HMO industry.
newsitem.headline: Shalala seeks to reassure U.S. HMO industry.

text.p: U.S. Health and Human Services Secretary Donna Shalala on Monday sought to reassure the managed health care industry that a proposed presidential panel would not attempt a sweeping overhaul of the health industry.

At a conference sponsored by the American Association of Health Plans, Shalala said the commission would be narrowly focused on the issues of consumer protection, health care quality, and the availability of treatment and services.
The commission would begin work if President Clinton wins a second term.

"This is not a panel that is organized to attack managed care," said Shalala, who noted that the number of Americans in managed care under the federal health programs Medicare and Medicaid have been growing rapidly.
She said the commission would aim for an initial report by September 1997 and make final recommendations about 18 months later.
Shalala said that in a time of rapid change in the health care system, the commission would look at the "ragged edges" but would not advocate large-scale overhauls.
